title: The First Real Job
description: Two offers on the table. Option A: A corporate role at a Fortune 500 company—good salary, prestige, benefits, but soul-crushing hours and a boss known for yelling. Option B: A nonprofit doing meaningful work—lower pay, mission-driven, but you'd believe in what you're doing. Your bank account whispers for A. Your heart whispers for B.

outcomes.narration: You take the corporate job. The first year is brutal—sixty-hour weeks, a screaming boss, anxiety before every meeting. But you climb. By year three, you're earning twice as much, managing people, driving a better car. Your student loans disappear. You have savings. You tell yourself the sacrifice was worth it. Some nights, you almost believe it.

choices.label: Follow your conscience to the nonprofit

outcomes.narration: You take the nonprofit job. The work matters—you can see it in the faces of the people you help. Paycheck is lean, but you stop dreading Mondays. Coworkers become friends. The mission fills something inside you. Money isn't everything. You learn that, and you're grateful for it.

choices.label: Try to create a third option

outcomes.narration: You ask the corporate job for remote work and a flexible schedule. To your surprise, they counter with a compromise—slightly less pay but four-day weeks. You take it. Best of both worlds—stability with room to breathe. Your negotiation skills paid off.
You try to negotiate but fumble. Both offers rescind. You're left with nothing, scrambling to find something new. The rejection stings, and the 'what if' haunts you.
